Years ago, it became clear to us that our customers' hardest problem would be coordinating work from beginning to end, and we started building for it. We bet on orchestration because that is where the challenge sits. A process has to exist in a form that agents and people can both act on, held and governed in one place, and coordinated with the systems doing the rest of the work. That layer is orchestration, and it is what we chose to build the
UiPath
Platform around.

Today, UiPath has been named a Leader in the
Gartner
Magic Quadrant™ for Business Orchestration and Automation Technologies. This one means a great deal to me. Execution is whether what we build holds up in production. Vision is whether we are building the right thing for what comes next. Being recognized in both says the direction was right, and that the market now sees it the same way.

Thank you to the UiPath team for the years of work behind this, and to our customers for trusting us.

You can read the full report here:

Automation Careers 2026: Skills You MUST Learn Now (YouTube Link in the Comments)

Is RPA dead?

Not exactly—but RPA alone is no longer enough. According to today's guest
Christopher Radich
, Public Sector CTO of
UiPath
The tech industry is rapidly shifting from simple rule-based automation to AI-powered, end-to-end automation systems.

That means roles like:
RPA Developer
Automation Engineer
AI Engineer

…are all evolving into something bigger.

👉 In this video, we break down the real future of automation careers and what skills actually matter in 2026 and beyond.

📌 In this video:
- Why RPA is still relevant (but limited)
- The shift from RPA → AI + Automation
- What companies actually want now (hint: not just RPA skills)
- Role of Large Language Models (LLMs) in automation
- Why data pipelines + ML models are becoming essential
- Difference between AI Engineer vs Automation Engineer
- How enterprise systems are integrating AI with workflows
- Why “agentic AI” is overhyped (real industry perspective)
- Skills you need to stay relevant in automation careers
- What hiring managers actually look for in 2026

- RPA is now just one tool in a bigger AI ecosystem.
- To stay relevant, you must learn:
Data integration

💡 Reality Check:
- If you only know how to build RPA scripts,
